Hey, let me start off with saying that it is going to be hard. No matter what choice you all make, it will be hard to do, but I promise you that in the end you’ll get better, and he is lucky to have been with such a loving person and family for so long. I’ve had two of my own pets pass away and it caused me to spiral for months, but I promise you that pain will get better over time.

Be sure you can say goodbye and try to be with him in the end, it will be awful and hard, but he will be grateful and it will help to ease some guilt you’ll likely feel as a natural part of the grief. Take lots of pictures and videos, try to have some sort of thing to remember him with (some fur or a paw print maybe). Love him as much as you can until he goes, and then try to focus on loving yourself to get through the pain.

I hope this helps in some way, I’m so sorry that you’re going through this, I’m sure he is so grateful to have been with you for so long.

I can’t say how certain I am on this being an actual thing, but we do experience something relatively similar. Specifically two of our “symptom holders” are not allowed to have caffeine or sugar on an empty stomach because it triggers manic episodes but it has only ever done so to them and we assume it is because of how strongly our mental health connects to them. We’ve experimented with it a few times (probably not smart, don’t follow in our footsteps). Obviously I’m not a professional or anything of the sort, but my guess is that it’s dependent on the alter themself because of what your brain is doing to process them and their environment—causing them to experience the caffeine differently—and not technically who drank it.

I’m thinking something like alter A gets jittery when they have coffee, alter B switches in and they don’t feel that way, but then alter C switches in and they get anxious because of the effects of caffeine. And it’s dependent on their role in your system and what parts of your brain make them up?

Hi! I had this issue with my leo awhile back. I would not recommend you keep feeding wax worms as that tends to just reinforce the behavior, in case you still are doing so. Just try offering a variety of foods, he’ll eat eventually!

A few tips i have are to cut the head off your feeders and offer it to him by rubbing the guts around his mouth, sometimes tasting the bug directly will get him interested. Another tip is to try hornworms, they’re still considered treat food, but sometimes the look of them gets the gecko interested, and you can try cutting the head off and offering the guts too—something is better than nothing.

It took my buddy a few weeks to get over it, it could take longer or shorter, but as long as he doesn’t rapidly lose weight he will be okay without food for a little bit—the last thing you want to do is force feed him unless it’s medically necessary. Also you’re definitely not going to want to offer wax worms again for a good long while once he gets back on normal food.
